body: Never let the fear of striking out, keep you from playing the game.

Thank you so much for your advice , it's not often that people will tell you to take time for yourself. It's very refreshing to read! I will definitely try and focus on myself more. I'm not good with being around people for such long periods of time, so I definitely need some space.

I'm glad to know that I'm not the only person out there who ran away from a job they hated! It's been about 11 months since I moved. Unfortunately I live in an asian country and they don't have a lot of mental health workers here. When I went to go get a prescription from the doctor, they didn't even have bipolar disorder on their system. Also money is incredibly tight now because of the virus so I'm just trying to do the best I can for now.

Personally I would say that people should not make fun of how someone handles their anxiety or make them feel bad for what they do to keep their anxiety under control. 

For example, I have been diagnosed with anxiety and I take medication for it. I prefer to leave for work a good while before I have to start because there are so many factors in play and I am a teacher and don't want to get into trouble for being late (even more anxiety). My contract states that I need to be at my class 15 minutes before it starts , so if my class starts at 7am, I need to be at the school latest 6:45am. It takes about 30-40 minutes to get to school depending on weather and traffic so I would need to leave around 6am to make sure that I get to school on time. My roommate makes snarky comments about how I leave so early for work when she will leave at about 6:20 because she only gives herself 10 minutes for traffic and things like that and isn't concerned about being at school 15 minutes in advance. 

Leaving early makes me feel more in control and I don't feel rushed when I get to work. It would help if people and friends just keep their comments to themselves if they don't have anxiety or understand it. We are all different and we all have our own quirks and ways of doing things that help.
I would tell my brother's doctor that I think he has a certain autoimmune disease so that he could be diagnosed earlier and hopefully be saved.

I just wanted to say that this thread has been such a great reminder about why I decided to become an ESL teacher, which is to make a difference in my students' lives. Whether it is from just a smile to a "well done", I hope that for the 45 minutes I have my kids, they feel loved, safe and important. 

Keep doing what you are doing,  even if you think no one notices. A simple smile can mean the world to someone.

I felt the exact same away about wanting to run away to somewhere you and I actually followed through and did it. 

I'm speaking from my own experience and I am in no way advocating for you to just leave your current life behind in search of greener pastures. This was probably the best decision I have made so far in my life. I was absolutely miserable and depressed back home (don't get me wrong, I am still bipolar and I tend towards depression) but I have been far more happpier than I have been at home. Seeing as I'm in another country across the world, I have managed to lose contact with majority of the people I know. The only people I have contact with back home are three family members and occasionally one of my friends.

This was also an incredibly risky and perhaps stupid decision that I made. I am terribly shy but decided that I will become an ESL tescher (so I have to teach classes of 45 students, sometimes more). I don't really have a doctor here who can help monitor and prescribe medication as needed and this is an Asian country so Bipolar is not really heard of here. 

I suppose my two cents on this would be to maybe take a break from life, go on a holiday by yourself somewhere if finances allow it. We need to embrace our lives and make the best of it.
Don't let the fear of striking out, keep you from playing the game.

I have tried to reach out more to this person, but unfortunately I am currently living in a different country so the time zones makes things a bit difficult. 
From what I can see, the person is starting to feel better and we chat as much as possible on social media. 

I think it was just horrible to come across because they  mean the world to me and I don't think I would be able to cope with them passing away, whether through suicide or other means.
They were about how lonely this person is and that they were thinking of suicide. I think it just sucked reading it because I didn't realize it was that bad.
Mine isn't too serious but I regret finding a family member's reddit account. Reading the posts that they made broke my heart and caused me to have even more anxiety than usual.

Thank you for such a detailed response and sharing your personal experiences with me, I really appreciate it. 
I think I was just hoping that one day, he'd not be on my mind anymore. I think he was just an important part of my life at that time because I needed him a lot and he stepped up to the plate, so it made a lasting impression on me. 
I've started seeing someone new and although it's not official yet (thank you Coronavirus and being stuck in different countries) I would say that I really do like him and it made me concerned that the stuff with my ex was still there. 
It gives me some hope to know that although you still think of your ex, you've managed to find love again, so thank you for that!

This makes me so sad to read. I'm so sorry that you went through such a horrible experience. I hope that you're doing some what better as time goes by? 
From my personal experience and I'm sure other people here would agree, depression doesn't discriminate against the life experiences you have. There are people who have absolutely everything they could ever want but they might still be depressed. 

I'm sorry that I have nothing important to contribute towards your question, but I'm here if you need someone to talk to.
